notes: Robots (200, 504 B) allows everything except /busca/ and advertises /sitemap/map/day/sitemap.xml, /sitemap/1.xml, /sitemap/2.xml. Tried the day sitemap first: 200, flat urlset with <lastmod> in -03:00, but it only holds the last ~6 days (1000 URLs, 10-21..10-27), so it cannot cover 09-25..10-25 alone; the script still reads it as a safety net (added 0). /sitemap/1.xml (200) and /sitemap/2.xml (200) are sitemapindexes of /sitemap/map/<N>.xml, N=1..1385, the highest N being the newest. Walked N downwards from 1385: each file is a flat urlset of <=1000 URLs whose entries run oldest->newest and whose <lastmod> span is contiguous with the neighbours (1385=10-25..10-27, 1384=10-20..10-25, 1383=10-15..10-20, 1382=10-10..10-15, 1381=10-06..10-10, 1380=10-01..10-06, 1379=09-28..10-01, 1378=09-23..09-28), so 8 files cover the whole 31-day window; the loop stops as soon as a file's oldest <lastmod> is before 2026-09-25. 10 requests, 12 s, well under the caps. Listed date = date part of <lastmod>, which is Brazil local (-03:00) and IS publication time: on 15 re-fetched articles (2 per target day plus 9 random across the window) JSON-LD datePublished matched the listed date exactly, 15/15, zero drift, and every page had 3.6k-23k characters of text. Dropped /blogs-redirect/ URLs: they are 401-character stub pages whose own page date is 2020-08-07 whatever the sitemap says (this is what the previous attempt listed and failed on). Result: 6377 unique URLs, 31/31 days, 09-30=251, 10-10=107, 10-20=231, min 103 on 09-26 (weekends are genuinely lower: 10-10 is a Saturday).
